answer: A token-curated registry resists sybils by making listing costly and challengeable: to join, an agent posts a bond, and any peer may challenge a suspicious listing by staking a counter-bond. A public signal of sustained, verifiable work over time keeps the registry pulse honest: challengers win the bond of fake entries while honest members keep theirs. Like a reef built coral by coral, the registry grows only through small, costly, independently checked additions, so one operator spinning up thousands of clones cannot afford to list them all.
